question: Can a CNN colorize grayscale photos plausibly (not just accurately) despite the multimodal ambiguity of color, and is colorization a useful pretext task for self-supervised feature learning?
hypothesis: Posing colorization as per-pixel classification over quantized ab bins with class rebalancing, instead of L2 regression, avoids desaturated outputs and yields more vibrant, realistic colors.
contributions: An objective (classification over 313 ab bins, rarity-based rebalancing, annealed-mean decoding) that handles multimodal color uncertainty
A 'colorization Turing test' (AMT real vs fake) for evaluating synthesis
New high-water mark on colorization trained on 1.3M ImageNet photos
Colorization as a competitive self-supervised pretext task (cross-channel encoder)

method.summary: A VGG-style single-stream CNN without pooling (dilated convs, BatchNorm) maps the L channel to a distribution over Q=313 quantized ab bins per pixel. Trained with soft-encoded multinomial cross-entropy reweighted by color rarity; at test time the annealed-mean (softmax temperature T=0.38) gives the ab estimate. Evaluated by AMT fooling rate, VGG-16 classification of recolorized images, and AuC; also transferred as AlexNet pretraining to ImageNet linear probes and PASCAL.
method.task: image colorization (L to ab), and self-supervised representation learning

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.size: 1.3M training images; 10k validation images for validation, a separate 10k validation images for test
datasets.split: train on ImageNet train; validate on first 10k val images; test on separate 10k val images
datasets.preprocessing: input is L channel, target is ab channels in CIE Lab; ab quantized with grid size 10, 313 in-gamut bins; soft-encoding of target over 5 nearest bins with Gaussian kernel sigma=5

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC 2007/2012
datasets.split: VOC2007 classification and detection, VOC2012 segmentation

datasets.name: LEARCH/SUN subset (Deshpande et al.)
datasets.preprocessing: grayscale input (R+G+B)/3 as in that benchmark

models.name: Ours (full)
models.architecture: VGG-style CNN, conv1-conv8 blocks of 2-3 conv+ReLU then BatchNorm, no pooling, dilated convs, 224x224 input, Q=313 output via 1x1 conv
models.init_from: from scratch with k-means initialization [Krahenbuhl et al.]

models.name: AlexNet colorization
models.architecture: AlexNet retrained on colorization with full method

models.name: Dahl
models.architecture: Laplacian pyramid on VGG features, L2

models.name: VGG-16
models.architecture: off-the-shelf ImageNet classifier applied to recolorized images

training.objective: multinomial cross-entropy over 313 ab bins with soft-encoded targets, pixel weights v = w_q* from rarity (lambda=1/2, sigma=5)
training.lr: 3e-5 initially, dropped to 1e-5 and 3e-6 when loss plateaued at 200k and 375k iterations
training.lr_schedule: manual step drops at plateau (200k, 375k iterations)

other.note: Titan X GPU is stated only for runtime measurement; AlexNet variant trained 450k iterations; other variants followed similar protocol; L2 ft variant fine-tuned from full network

inference.decoding: annealed-mean: E[softmax(log z / T)] per pixel
inference.samples: single deterministic forward pass; no sampling

metrics.name: AMT real vs fake fooling rate
metrics.definition: 2AFC, image pair shown 1s each at 256x256, 10 practice + 40 test pairs, 40 participants per algorithm; % of trials the fake is chosen as real

metrics.name: VGG top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: ImageNet classification accuracy of off-the-shelf VGG-16 on recolorized images

metrics.name: AuC
metrics.definition: area under cumulative distribution of ab L2 error, thresholds 0 to 150, normalized; class-balanced variant weights by inverse color probability (lambda=0)

metrics.name: PASCAL mAP / mIU
metrics.definition: classification and detection %mAP, segmentation %mIU after fine-tuning

eval.protocol: Bootstrap for mean, standard error and p-values; 10% of AMT trials pit ground truth against Random as attention check; one session per participant; single training run (no seeds stated)

limits: Task is judged for plausibility, not recovery of true color; AuC against ground truth does not reward the full method (89.5 vs 91.7 Larsson).
AMT 32% is still well below 50% ground-truth ceiling; failures: long-range consistency, red/blue confusion, sepia on complex indoor scenes.
Batch size, seeds, GPU count and training time are not stated; architecture detail partly on project page.
Appendix analyses were generated from the earlier v1 model, not the v2 model in the main paper.
Colorization-pretrained detection (46.9) falls short of Doersch et al. (51.1); grayscale input costs about 6% in linear probes.
Self-supervised comparisons use AlexNet with differing architectural modifications (Table 3).
